realtime.title: Realtime
realtime.field_hint: Matches literal keys first, then nested paths such as app.name.
realtime.fallback_hint: Where an event goes when the field is missing, is not text, or does not make a stream name.
realtime.auto_create: A stream that does not exist yet is created by the first event written to it.
realtime.retain_hint: Keep the original log in {{source}} after routing (masking still applies). Write once when source and destination match.
realtime.no_backfill: Realtime pipelines run on intake and do not support backfill.

processing.output_hint: The routing step chooses the stream for each event. A stream that does not exist yet is created by the first event written to it.

settings.reliability_hint: A failed read or write is retried on the same stretch of time after 30 s, then twice as long each time up to the run interval, and skipped when the retries run out; a failed delivery is retried within the run. Events a step fails on, a stream rejects or a connector does not take go to the dead letter stream (logs) with the stage and the reason. Dedupe works within one run.
settings.realtime_note: Runs on every log event as it is ingested: one source stream, one destination, no schedule.

flow.no_steps: No steps: events are written as they are read.

editor.source_hint: Each run reads this stream from where the last one stopped. The first run reaches back as far as "First run reads back" says.
editor.source_realtime_hint: Every event written to this stream goes through the steps as it arrives. The stream may not exist yet.
editor.copy_hint: Every event is written here too, whatever the routing step picks. The stream is created by the first event written to it.
editor.connector_hint: Every event the pipeline writes is also delivered to this connector.
editor.connector_none: This workspace has no connectors yet.
editor.save_vrl_invalid: A step is not valid VRL. Run a test to see which one, and why.

processors.path_hint: Dots reach into nested objects: user.email is email inside user.
processors.target_hint: Leave empty to merge the parsed keys into the event.
processors.pattern_hint: Named groups become fields, for example (?P<status>\d+).
processors.convert_hint: A value that cannot be converted is left as it is.
processors.filter_number_hint: A number, or text that reads as one; any other value does not match.
processors.sample_percent_hint: Above 0 and up to 100; decimals are fine.
processors.sample_by_hint: Events with the same value are all kept or all dropped, such as one trace. Leave it blank to pick events at random.

test.title: Test
test.subtitle: One event through every step. Nothing is stored.
test.sample_invalid: The sample is not valid JSON.
test.hint: Edit the sample to look like your data, then run it to see what the steps make of it.
test.stale: The steps changed since this run.
test.failed_note: When the pipeline runs, an event that fails a step counts as failed, and goes to the dead letter stream when there is one.
test.dropped_note: The event is dropped on purpose and goes nowhere; a run counts it as dropped, not as failed.
test.no_recent: No events in {{stream}} in the last 24 hours.
test.no_steps: This pipeline has no steps: the event is written as it is.

connectors.title: Connectors
connectors.subtitle: How logs come in from other services, and where pipelines deliver what they write.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Logs brought in from another service and written to a stream.

destinations.title: Destinations
destinations.description: Where a pipeline can deliver its output, beside the stream it writes.

kind_hints.aws_cloudwatch_logs: MoleSignal fetches a log group on a timer.
kind_hints.aws_kinesis_firehose: A Firehose stream pushes its records here.
kind_hints.cloudflare_logpush: A Logpush job pushes request logs here.
kind_hints.heroku_drain: An app's log drain pushes its lines here.
kind_hints.s3: Each batch a pipeline writes becomes a JSON Lines object in a bucket. Also for MinIO, R2, OSS and other S3-compatible stores.
kind_hints.kafka: Each event a pipeline writes becomes a message on a topic.

hints.access_key: A long-lived key of an IAM user. Give that user only what this connector needs.
hints.temporary_key: A short-lived key from AWS STS, valid only together with its session token. It stops working when it expires and has to be replaced here.
hints.node_role: No key is stored. MoleSignal uses the role of the machine it runs on (an EC2 instance profile), which needs s3:PutObject on the bucket.
hints.sasl_plain: SASL/PLAIN. The connection is not encrypted, so use it on a private network only: TLS and SCRAM are not supported yet.
hints.none: For a broker that asks for no credentials. The connection is not encrypted.
hints.push_token: The other service presents this token with every push. Whoever holds it can write to the stream.

hints.target_stream: A stream that does not exist yet is created by the first event.
hints.region_s3: The bucket's region. An S3-compatible store may not need one.
hints.brokers: Host and port. Separate several with commas.
hints.endpoint: The store's S3 API address, starting with http:// or https://.

compatible.hint: For MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Alibaba Cloud OSS and others that speak the S3 API.
compatible.virtual_hosted: Address the bucket as a host name
compatible.virtual_hosted_hint: Some stores, Alibaba Cloud OSS among them, do not take the bucket in the path.

secret.saved: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
secret.retype: This server does not keep a saved secret when a connector is changed. Enter it again to save.

problems.endpoint_invalid: The endpoint has to start with http:// or https://.
problems.push_token_short: The token needs at least 16 characters.

push.title: Point {{kind}} here
push.once: The token is shown this once. Copy it now: it cannot be read back later, only replaced.
push.saved_token: A token is saved. It cannot be shown again.
push.no_token: No token yet, so nothing it is sent is accepted.
push.regenerated: A new token is ready. It replaces the current one when you save, and is shown once after that.

steps.aws_kinesis_firehose: In the Firehose stream, choose the HTTP endpoint destination. Enter the endpoint as its URL and the token as its access key.
steps.cloudflare_logpush: Create a Logpush job with this HTTP destination. The token travels in a header Cloudflare adds to every push.
steps.heroku_drain: Add the drain to your app. Heroku cannot send a header, so the token travels in the address.

push.will_generate: A token is generated when the connector is created, and shown once.

remove.title: Delete {{name}}?
remove.source: Logs stop arriving from it. What it already wrote stays in the stream.
remove.destination: A pipeline that still delivers to it records an error on every run until the connector is taken out of it.

connectors.toggle_retype: This server cannot switch a connector without its secrets being entered again. Open it to change it.
connectors.unknown_kind: A kind this version does not know: {{kind}}
